memory_candidates.content: When reading a count+max (or any numeric aggregate) out of jq -R -s into a bash variable via command substitution, always add -r. Without -r, jq -R -s emits a JSON-quoted string (e.g. '"2 17"'), and a subsequent `awk '{print $1}'` split produces a field with a leading quote character, which then silently evaluates as 0 in numeric awk comparisons -- making every non-trivial case look like it fell below a threshold/floor. Caught only by running the full set of fixture directions (light, heavy, edge, malformed) and finding ALL of them misclassified the same way.

To commit a one-hunk fix to a shared, ledger-style file (e.g. an index/line-count manifest) when a concurrent sibling task holds its own unstaged edits to the SAME file: (1) back up the full working-tree content to a scratch path in a dedicated bash call; (2) in a SEPARATE bash call, overwrite the working file with the already-staged index blob (`git show :path > path`) so working tree == index for that path; (3) commit via the scoped script; (4) restore the backup. Both `git commit -- <path>` and `git add <path>` take the CURRENT WORKING-TREE content of the named path, not whatever is already staged -- verified directly in a scratch repo. CRITICAL: steps 1 and 2 must be genuinely separate tool calls, never combined in one multi-line bash invocation -- a PreToolUse destructive-git guard can block the WHOLE call atomically before step 1's backup ever executes, while a later non-git overwrite line in that same call still runs, destroying the sibling's unstaged work with no backup in place.

Pattern for demoting a static category/family membership test from *verdict* to *candidacy pre-filter*, backed by a measured signal with a conservative no-history fallback: (1) keep the family array as the first gate (answers 'could this even apply?'); (2) add a measured signal as the second gate (answers 'does it, in fact?'); (3) aggregate with max (never mean) when the risk is one-sided (a thing that was ever heavy can be heavy again; a thing that was only ever light may simply not have hit its heavy path yet); (4) require a minimum sample count before trusting a *light* verdict; (5) default to the conservative (heavy) verdict whenever no usable history exists, so the change is strictly a relaxation applied only where evidence exists, never new exposure. Reusable whenever replacing a static category-based admission rule with a measured one.
